units.zh: 末帝將圖起義，為捍禦之備，延朗計公私粟帛，以贍其急。
units.en: When the Last Emperor was planning to raise an uprising and made preparations for defense, Yanlang calculated public and private grain and cloth to supply the urgent need.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor was planning to raise an uprising and made preparations for defense, Yanlang calculated public and private grain and cloth to supply the urgent need.

units.zh: 及西師納降，末帝赴洛，皆無所闕焉，末帝甚賞之。
units.en: When the western army submitted and the Last Emperor went to Luoyang, nothing was lacking in any respect, and the Last Emperor greatly rewarded him.
units.literal: When the western army submitted and the Last Emperor went to Luoyang, nothing was lacking in any respect, and the Last Emperor greatly rewarded him.

units.zh: 清泰初，除宣徽北院使，俄以劉延皓守鄴，改副樞密使，累官至檢校太傅。
units.en: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Domestic Service; soon, because Liu Yanhao was intendant at Ye, he was changed to deputy commissioner of military affairs and rose in succession to acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Domestic Service; soon, because Liu Yanhao was intendant at Ye, he was changed to deputy commissioner of military affairs and rose in succession to acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 時房皓為樞密使，但高枕閑眠，啟奏除授，一歸延朗，由是得志。
units.en: At that time Fang Hao was commissioner of military affairs but only rested his head high and slept at leisure; memorials for appointments and dismissals all went to Yanlang, and thereby he got his way.
units.literal: At that time Fang Hao was commissioner of military affairs but only rested his head high and slept at leisure; memorials for appointments and dismissals all went to Yanlang, and thereby he got his way.

units.zh: 凡藩侯郡牧，自外入者，必先賂延朗，後議進貢，賂厚者先居內地，賂薄者晚出邊藩，故諸將屢有怨訕，末帝不能察之。
units.en: Whenever frontier lords and prefects came in from outside, they had first to bribe Yanlang and only afterward discuss advancing tribute; those who bribed heavily were first placed in inner territories, those who bribed lightly were sent out late to border commands—therefore the generals often had resentful complaints, which the Last Emperor could not perceive.
units.literal: Whenever frontier lords and prefects came in from outside, they had first to bribe Yanlang and only afterward discuss advancing tribute; those who bribed heavily were first placed in inner territories, those who bribed lightly were sent out late to border commands—therefore the generals often had resentful complaints, which the Last Emperor could not perceive.

units.zh: 及晉高祖入洛，延朗將竄於南山，與從者數輩，過其私第，指而歎曰：「我有錢三十萬貫聚於此，不知為何人所得。」
units.en: When the Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanlang was about to flee into the southern mountains; with several followers he passed his private residence, pointed at it, and sighed, "I have three hundred thousand strings of cash gathered here—I do not know who will obtain it."
units.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanlang was about to flee into the southern mountains; with several followers he passed his private residence, pointed at it, and sighed, "I have three hundred thousand strings of cash gathered here—I do not know who will obtain it."

units.zh: 其愚暗如此。
units.en: His foolish darkness was such as this.
units.literal: His foolish darkness was such as this.

units.zh: 尋捕而殺之。
units.en: Soon he was captured and killed.
units.literal: Soon he was captured and killed.

units.zh: 然自此權臣愎戾，伶官用事，吏人孔謙酷加賦斂，赦文之所原放，謙復刻剝不行，大失人心，始於此矣。
units.en: Yet from then on ministers turned stubborn, actors held power, and Kong Qian re-levied what the amnesty had freed—hearts were lost from this day.
units.literal: Yet from this time powerful ministers grew obstinate, actor-officials held office, and clerk Kong Qian harshly added levies; what the amnesty had remitted Qian again exacted and would not carry out—greatly losing hearts, it began here.

units.zh: 庚午，租庸使孔謙奏：「諸道綱運客旅，多於私路苟免商稅，請令所在關防嚴加捉搦。」
units.en: On gengwu Kong Qian memorialized, "Transport convoys and traveling merchants on the circuits often evade commercial tax on private routes; order every pass and barrier to seize them strictly."
units.literal: On gengwu land-tax commissioner Kong Qian memorialized: "Transport convoys and traveling merchants on the circuits often evade commercial tax on private routes; order every pass and barrier to seize them strictly."

units.zh: 以北京副留守馮贇為宣徽使、判三司。
units.en: Beijing deputy regent Feng Yun became palace treasury commissioner and revenue overseer.
units.literal: Beijing deputy regent Feng Yun was made Palace Treasury Commissioner and overseer of the Revenue Commission.

units.zh: 因召吳珙、李存璋、李存敬、朱守殷諭其謀，眾鹹憤怒。
units.en: He called Wu Gong, Li Cunzhang, Li Cunjing, and Zhu Shouyin; all raged.
units.literal: He then summoned Wu Gong, Li Cunzhang, Li Cunjing, and Zhu Shouyin to explain the plot; all were furious.

units.zh: 二月壬戌，命存璋伏甲以誅克寧，遂靖其難。
units.en: On renxu in the second month Cunzhang ambushed and killed Kening, ending the crisis.
units.literal: On renxu in the second month he ordered Cunzhang with hidden armor to execute Kening and thus settled the trouble.

units.zh: 己巳，秘書少監姚顗為左散騎常侍，以太子左諭德陸崇為右散騎常侍，以兵部郎中蕭希甫為左諫議大夫，前幽州節度判官呂夢奇為右諫議大夫，以鄴都副留守孫嶽為潁州團練使。
units.en: On jisi Yao Hui became Left Regular Attendant; crown prince mentor Lu Chong became Right Regular Attendant; Xiao Xifu of Military Affairs became Left Remonstrator; Lü Mengqi, former Youzhou aide, became Right Remonstrator; Sun Yue, Yedu deputy regent, became Ying training commissioner.
units.literal: On jisi, Vice Director of the Secretariat Yao Hui was made Left Regular Attendant; the crown prince's Left Mentor Lu Chong was made Right Regular Attendant; Bureau of Military Affairs director Xiao Xifu was made Left Remonstrator; former Youzhou military commissioner's aide Lü Mengqi was made Right Remonstrator; Yedu deputy regent Sun Yue was made Yingzhou training commissioner.

units.zh: 以鄴都副留守、興唐尹張憲檢校吏部尚書、太原尹，充北京副留守、知留守事。
units.en: Zhang Xian—Yedu deputy regent and Xingtang prefect—became acting Personnel minister, Taiyuan prefect, and northern deputy regent in charge of regency.
units.literal: Yedu deputy regent and Xingtang prefect Zhang Xian was made acting Minister of Personnel, Taiyuan prefect, and northern capital deputy regent with charge of regency affairs.

units.zh: 陝州節度使張延朗移鎮許州，加檢校太傅；
units.en: Zhang Yanlang of Shaan moved to Xu with inspector grand mentor rank;
units.literal: Shaan prefecture military commissioner Zhang Yanlang was transferred to Xu prefecture and given added Inspector Grand Mentor;

units.zh: 張彥之亂，命判官王正言草奏，正言素不能文，不能下筆，彥怒詬曰：「鈍漢乃辱我！」
units.en: When Zhang Yan rebelled he ordered his aide Wang Zhengyan to draft a memorial, but Wang, who had never mastered prose, could not write a word; Zhang Yan thundered, "You blockheaded oaf—how dare you disgrace me!"
units.literal: During Zhang Yan's rebellion, he ordered the secretary Wang Zhengyan to draft the memorial; Zhengyan had never been able to write and could not set brush to paper; Yan angrily cursed him: "You dull-witted Han—how dare you shame me!"

units.zh: 頲揮筆成文，詆斥梁君臣，彥甚喜，為判官。
units.en: Ting wrote at speed, the draft lashing out at Liang sovereign and ministers; Zhang Yan was delighted and kept him as his secretary.
units.literal: Ting swept his brush and completed the text, denouncing the Liang ruler and ministers; Yan was greatly pleased and made him secretary.

units.zh: 及張彥復脅賀德倫降於唐，德倫遣頲先奉狀太原。
units.en: When Zhang Yan once more forced He Delun to surrender to Tang, Delun sent Ting ahead to Taiyuan with the formal submission.
units.literal: When Zhang Yan again coerced He Delun to surrender to Tang, Delun sent Ting first to present the submission at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 王緘，幽州劉仁恭故吏也。
units.en: Wang Jian had been a clerk in the service of Liu Rengong of Youzhou.
units.literal: Wang Jian was a former clerk of Liu Rengong of Youzhou.

units.zh: 〈（《契丹國誌·韓延徽傳》：延徽自契丹奔晉，晉王欲置之幕府掌書記，王緘嫉之，延徽不自安，求東歸省母，遂復入契丹，寓書於晉王，敘所以北去之意。
units.en: (Khitan State Records, Biography of Han Yanhui: Yanhui fled the Khitan for Jin; the Prince of Jin wished to make him chief secretary. Wang Jian resented him; uneasy in Taiyuan, Yanhui asked leave to visit his mother in the east, returned to the Khitan, and wrote the prince explaining why he had gone north.
units.literal: (Khitan State Records, Biography of Han Yanhui: Yanhui fled from Khitan to Jin; the Prince of Jin wished to place him in the staff office as chief secretary. Wang Jian envied him; Yanhui was ill at ease, asked to go east to visit his mother, and thus re-entered Khitan. He sent a letter to the Prince of Jin explaining why he went north.

units.zh: 且曰：「非不戀英主，非不思故鄉，所以不留，正懼王緘之讒耳。」）〉
units.en: He wrote, "It is not that I do not love an enlightened master or long for home; I dare not stay because I fear Wang Jian's slander.")〉
units.literal: He also said: "It is not that I do not cherish an enlightened lord, nor that I do not think of my homeland; the reason I do not stay is precisely that I fear Wang Jian's slander.")〉

units.zh: 每於公宴，但呼王緘而已。
units.en: At every public feast he would call only "Wang Jian" and use no other name for him.
units.literal: At every public banquet he would only call out "Wang Jian" and nothing more.

units.zh: 緘堅辭復命，書詞稍抗，武皇怒，下獄詰之，謝罪聽命，乃署為推官，曆掌書記。
units.en: Jian insisted on returning to complete his mission; his letter was defiant in tone. The Martial Emperor in anger threw him into prison and questioned him. Jian apologized and submitted; he was named investigating officer and later chief secretary.
units.literal: Jian firmly declined to return to his commission; his letter's wording was somewhat defiant. The Martial Emperor was angry, put him in prison and interrogated him; he apologized and obeyed orders, and was then appointed investigating officer and successively served as chief secretary.

units.zh: 緘博學善屬文，燕薊多文士，緘後生，未知名，及在太原，名位驟達。
units.en: Jian was erudite and a fine writer; Yan and Ji had many men of letters, and Jian as a younger man was still unknown—at Taiyuan his name and rank rose overnight.
units.literal: Jian was broadly learned and skilled at composing text; Yan and Ji had many literary men. Jian was younger and not yet known by name; once he was at Taiyuan, fame and rank rose swiftly.

units.zh: 燕人馬鬱，有盛名於鄉里，而緘素以吏職事鬱。
units.en: Ma Yu of Yan enjoyed great local fame, though Jian had long served him in a clerk's capacity.
units.literal: Ma Yu of Yan had great fame in his home district, while Jian had long served Yu in a clerk's post.

units.zh: 及鬱在太原，謂緘曰：「公在此作文士，所謂避風之鳥，受賜於魯人也。」
units.en: When Yu came to Taiyuan he told Jian, "You play the literary man here—the bird that flees the storm and finds shelter with a stranger in Lu."
units.literal: When Yu was at Taiyuan he said to Jian: "You serve here as a literary man—the so-called bird that flees the wind and receives favor from the man of Lu."

units.zh: 十年，從征幽州，既獲仁恭父子，莊宗命緘為露布，觀其旨趣。
units.en: In the tenth year he marched on Youzhou; after Rengong and his sons were taken, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Jian to draft the victory bulletin to see where his loyalties lay.
units.literal: In the tenth year he followed the campaign against Youzhou; after Rengong father and son were captured, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Jian to draft the victory bulletin to observe his intent.

units.zh: 緘起草無所辭避，義士以此少之。
units.en: Jian wrote the bulletin without hesitation or evasion, and men of honor thought less of him for it.
units.literal: Jian drafted it without any evasion or refusal; men of honor therefore thought somewhat less of him.

units.zh: 胡柳之役，緘隨輜重前行，歿於亂兵。
units.en: At the battle of Huliu, Jian marched with the baggage train ahead of the column and was killed in the rout.
units.literal: In the battle at Huliu, Jian followed the baggage train forward and perished among the disorderly troops.

units.zh: 既而緘凶問至，莊宗流涕久之，得其喪，歸葬太原。
units.en: Word of Jian's death soon arrived; Emperor Zhuangzong wept a long while, recovered the body, and had it buried at Taiyuan.
units.literal: Soon word of Jian's death arrived; Emperor Zhuangzong wept for a long time, recovered his coffin, and returned it for burial at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 從莊宗經略山東，承製授檢校司空、魏博節度使。
units.en: He followed Emperor Zhuangzong in the pacification of Shandong and received by imperial order the acting title Minister of Works and the post of military commissioner of Weibo.
units.literal: Following Emperor Zhuangzong in pacifying Shandong, he received by imperial order appointment as Acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of Weibo.

units.zh: 少以刀筆直記室，仁恭假以幕職，令使鳳翔。
units.en: As a youth he served as recorder in Rengong's secretariat; the lord gave him a staff post and sent him on a mission to Fengxiang.
units.literal: In youth he served as recorder with brush and knife; Rengong lent him a staff post and sent him as envoy to Fengxiang.

units.zh: 際晚，盧質還營，莊宗問副使所在，曰：「某醉不之知也。」
units.en: Near evening Lu Zhi returned to camp; the emperor asked where the deputy commissioner was, and Lu said, "I was drunk and do not know."
units.literal: Near evening Lu Zhi returned to camp; Emperor Zhuangzong asked where the deputy commissioner was, and he said: "I was drunk and do not know."

units.zh: 還經太原，屬仁恭阻命，武皇留之。
units.en: On his return he passed through Taiyuan; Rengong had meanwhile defied the court, and the Martial Emperor detained him.
units.literal: Returning he passed through Taiyuan; it happened that Rengong blocked his orders, and the Martial Emperor detained him.

units.zh: 壬子，天雄軍屯駐捧聖都虞候張令昭逐其節度使劉延皓。
units.en: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao, deputy of the Bearer-of-Sagacity command at the Tianxiong encampment, drove out his military governor Liu Yanhao.
units.literal: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao, deputy commander of the Bearer-of-Sagacity command in the Tianxiong army garrison, expelled his military governor Liu Yanhao.

units.zh: 壬子，張令昭伏誅。
units.en: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao was put to death.
units.literal: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao was executed.

units.zh: 六月癸亥，以令昭為右千牛衛將軍，權知天雄軍事。
units.en: On guihai of the sixth month Lingzhao was made a general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and left in temporary charge of Tianxiong.
units.literal: In the sixth month, on guihai, Lingzhao was made general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and given acting authority over Tianxiong military affairs.

units.zh: 佗命官不書「以」，此書「以」者，明令昭猶可「以」。
units.en: Other appointments do not use the word “by.” It is used here to show that Lingzhao could still be appointed.
units.literal: Other appointments do not write “by appointing”; this writes “by appointing” to make clear that Lingzhao could still be appointed.

units.zh: 辛巳，以前相州刺史孟鵠為左驍衛大將軍，充三司使。
units.en: On xinsi former Xiangzhou inspector Meng Hu became left valiant guard senior general and three departments commissioner.
units.literal: On xinsi former Xiangzhou inspector Meng Hu was made Left Valiant Guard senior general and Commissioner of the Three Departments.

units.zh: 李襲吉，自言左相林甫之後，父圖，為洛陽令，因家焉。
units.en: Li Xiji claimed descent from the Left Chancellor Li Linfu. His father Tu served as magistrate of Luoyang, and the family made their home there.
units.literal: Li Xiji claimed for himself that he was a descendant of Left Chancellor Li Linfu; his father Tu was magistrate of Luoyang, and the family settled there.

units.zh: 襲吉乾符末應進士舉，遇亂，避地河中，依節度使李都，擢為鹽鐵判官。
units.en: Near the end of the Qianfu reign Xiji entered the jinshi examinations, but with rebellion abroad he fled to Hezhong and entered the service of Military Commissioner Li Du, who raised him to salt-and-iron judge.
units.literal: At the end of the Qianfu era Xiji sat for the jinshi examination; he encountered turmoil, fled to Hezhong, relied on Military Commissioner Li Du, and was promoted to salt-and-iron judge.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：習吉從李克用至渭南，令其入奏，帝重其文章，授諫議大夫，使上事北省以榮之。）〉
units.en: (Northern Dreams, Trivial Tales: Xiji accompanied Li Keyong to Weinan and was sent to present a memorial at court. The emperor prized his prose, named him Remonstrance Grand Master, and had him report to the northern secretariat as a mark of honor.)
units.literal: (Northern Dreams, Trivial Tales: Xiji followed Li Keyong to Weinan; the prince had him enter court with a memorial. The emperor valued his writings, appointed him Remonstrance Grand Master, and had him report to the northern secretariat to honor him.)

units.zh: 襲吉訪舊至太原，武皇署為府掾，出宰榆社。
units.en: Xiji followed old ties to Taiyuan, where the Martial Emperor Li Keyong named him a headquarters aide and later sent him out to govern Yushe county.
units.literal: Xiji, visiting old acquaintances, came to Taiyuan; the Martial Emperor appointed him a staff officer of the commandery and sent him out as magistrate of Yushe.

units.zh: 或有薦襲吉能文，召試稱旨，即署為掌書記。
units.en: Someone praised Xiji's literary gifts; summoned for a trial draft, he pleased the prince at once and was named chief secretary on the spot.
units.literal: Someone recommended that Xiji was skilled at writing; he was summoned for a trial and pleased the ruler, and was immediately appointed chief secretary.

units.zh: 三年，遷節度副使，從討王行瑜，拜右諫議大夫。
units.en: In the third year of his service he became deputy military commissioner, marched against Wang Xingyu, and received appointment as Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to deputy military commissioner, followed the campaign against Wang Xingyu, and was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

units.zh: 襲吉博學多通，尤諳悉國朝近事，為文精意練實，動據典故，無所放縱，羽檄軍書，辭理宏健。
units.en: Xiji was erudite and widely read, with a specialist's grasp of recent court history. His prose was tight and concrete, every line anchored in precedent, never florid; whether drafting battle orders or field reports, his style was vigorous and commanding.
units.literal: Xiji was broadly learned and widely versed, especially well acquainted with recent affairs of the dynasty; in writing he refined his meaning and condensed substance, constantly citing precedents without license, and in urgent dispatches and military documents his rhetoric was grand and forceful.

units.zh: 及師還渭北，武皇不獲入覲，為武皇作違離表，中有警句云：「穴禽有翼，聽舜樂以猶來；
units.en: When the army withdrew north of the Wei, the Martial Emperor was denied an imperial audience. Xiji wrote his master's petition of separation, with lines that ran: "Even a bird that nests in caves will spread its wings; hearing the music of Shun, it would still return;
units.literal: When the army returned to the north of the Wei, the Martial Emperor could not gain an audience; Xiji drafted for him a memorial on being kept apart, containing striking lines that read: "The cave-dwelling bird has wings; hearing Shun's music it would still return;

units.zh: 天復中，武皇議欲修好於梁，命襲吉為書以貽梁祖，書曰：
units.en: During the Tianfu reign the Martial Emperor resolved to reopen relations with Liang and charged Xiji to draft a letter to the Liang Founder. It read:
units.literal: In the Tianfu era the Martial Emperor deliberated on restoring good relations with Liang and ordered Xiji to draft a letter to the Liang Founder; the letter read:

units.zh: 昭宗覽之嘉歎。
units.en: Emperor Zhaozong read the memorial and sighed in admiration.
units.literal: Emperor Zhaozong read it and sighed in admiration.

units.zh: 洎襲吉入奏，麵詔諭之，優賜特異。
units.en: When Xiji presented the memorial in person, the emperor received him with a personal audience and lavished extraordinary gifts upon him.
units.literal: When Xiji came in to present the memorial, the emperor addressed him face to face and bestowed exceptional favors.

units.zh: 光啟初，武皇遇難上源，記室歿焉，既歸鎮，辟掌奏者，多不如旨。
units.en: Early in the Guangqi reign the Martial Emperor suffered the Shangyuan debacle, and his chief recorder died in the affair. Back in his headquarters he tried one memorialist after another, but few could satisfy him.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Guangqi era the Martial Emperor met disaster at Shangyuan and his recorder died there; after he returned to his command, those he recruited to manage memorials mostly failed to please him.

units.zh: 自武皇上源之難，與梁祖不協，乾寧末，劉仁恭負恩，其間論列是非，交相聘答者數百篇，警策之句，播在人口，文士稱之。
units.en: From the Shangyuan crisis through the rupture with the Liang Founder and, late in Qianning, Liu Rengong's betrayal, Xiji drafted hundreds of letters debating blame and merit between the rival camps. His sharpest lines passed from mouth to mouth, and men of letters spoke of him with admiration.
units.literal: From the Martial Emperor's Shangyuan disaster, through his breach with the Liang Founder and, at the end of Qianning, Liu Rengong's ingratitude, in the exchanges that argued right and wrong back and forth there were several hundred pieces; striking lines spread on people's lips, and literary men praised them.

units.zh: 天路無梯，望堯雲而不到。」
units.en: yet the road to Heaven has no ladder, and though one gazes at the clouds of Yao, one cannot reach them."
units.literal: the road to Heaven has no ladder; gazing at Yao's clouds one cannot arrive."

units.zh: 其年十二月，師還太原，王珂為浮梁於夏陽渡，襲吉從軍，時笮斷航破，武皇僅免，襲吉墜河，得大冰承足，沿流七八里，還岸而止，救之獲免。
units.en: That December, as the army marched back to Taiyuan, Wang Ke threw a pontoon bridge across the Xiayang ford and Xiji went with the column. The bridge cables snapped mid-crossing; the Martial Emperor barely escaped with his life. Xiji plunged into the river, caught a great slab of ice underfoot, and drifted seven or eight li downstream before he could claw his way ashore and be pulled out alive.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of that year the army returned to Taiyuan; Wang Ke built a pontoon bridge at Xiayang Ford and Xiji followed the campaign. At the time the bridge cables broke and the crossing was destroyed; the Martial Emperor barely escaped. Xiji fell into the river, found a great floe of ice to bear his feet, drifted with the current seven or eight li, stopped when he reached the bank, and was rescued and spared.

units.zh: 一別清德，十有餘年，失意杯盤，爭鋒劍戟。
units.en: Since we parted in mutual regard, more than ten years have passed—shared cups turned to estrangement, and blades crossed in place of toasts.
units.literal: Once we parted in pure virtue, more than ten years have passed; cups and dishes brought disappointment, and swords and spears vied in clash.

units.zh: 山長水闊，難追二國之歡；
units.en: Mountains lie between us and rivers run wide, so the old warmth of two allied states is hard to recover;
units.literal: mountains stretch long and waters spread wide, hard to recover the joy of two states;

units.zh: 雁逝魚沉，久絕八行之賜。
units.en: the wild goose is gone and the fish lies sunk in the deep—your eight-line letters have long ceased to come.
units.literal: wild geese have flown off and fish sunk deep, and for long the gift of an eight-line letter has been cut off.

units.zh: 比者仆與公實聯宗姓，原忝恩行，投分深情，將期棲托，論交馬上，薦美朝端，傾向仁賢，未省疏闕。
units.en: Not long ago we were bound by clan ties and I was unworthy of your kindness; we pledged our hearts to each other and looked to shelter under the same roof, struck up friendship in the saddle, praised each other at court, and leaned toward what was humane and worthy—I never thought you distant.
units.literal: Of late your servant and you were in truth linked by clan name, and I was unworthy of your gracious conduct; we pledged deep affection and looked to shelter together, made friends on horseback, praised each other at court, and inclined toward the humane and worthy—I never perceived any neglect.

units.zh: 豈謂運由奇特，謗起奸邪。
units.en: Who could have foreseen that fate would take so strange a turn, and that slander would rise from the wicked?
units.literal: Who would have said that fate arose from the strange, and slander rose from the wicked?

units.zh: 毒手尊拳，交相於幕夜；
units.en: Poisonous hands and clenched fists met under cover of night;
units.literal: poisonous hands and honored fists were exchanged in the curtain of night;

units.zh: 金戈鐵馬，蹂踐於明時。
units.en: golden spears and iron horses trampled the bright age itself.
units.literal: golden spears and iron horses trampled and trod in the bright age.

units.zh: 狂藥致其失歡，陳事止於堪笑。
units.en: Rash acts born of wine broke our good feeling; the incidents you cite are fit only for laughter.
units.literal: Mad medicine caused the loss of good feeling; the matters set forth ended only in what could be laughed at.

units.zh: 今則皆登貴位，盡及中年，蘧公亦要知非，君子何勞用壯。
units.en: Now we both stand in high office and have reached middle age; even Duke Qu of old came to know his mistake—why should gentlemen still strain their prime?
units.literal: Now we have all ascended to exalted rank and all reached middle age; even Duke Qu must know his error—why should a gentleman trouble to use his prime strength?

units.zh: 今公貴先列辟，名過古人。
units.en: You now outrank the feudal lords of the age, and your fame surpasses the ancients.
units.literal: Now you are honored before the feudal lords of the age, and your fame surpasses the ancients.

units.zh: 合縱連衡，本務家邦之計；
units.en: Vertical alliances and horizontal leagues are fundamentally plans for house and state;
units.literal: to ally vertically and join horizontally is fundamentally a plan for one's house and state;

units.zh: 拓地守境，要存子孫之基。
units.en: to expand territory and hold your borders is to preserve a foundation for your sons and grandsons.
units.literal: to expand territory and guard borders is to preserve the foundation for one's sons and grandsons.

units.zh: 文王貴奔走之交，仲尼譚損益之友，仆顧慚虛薄，舊忝眷私，一言許心，萬死不悔，壯懷忠力，猶勝他人，盟於三光，願赴湯火。
units.en: King Wen prized friends who came running at his call; Confucius spoke of companions who could tell gain from loss. I know myself shallow and unworthy, yet I was once honored with your private regard; one pledged word bound my heart, and I would not repent though I died ten thousand deaths. My loyal strength still outmatches other men; I swear by sun, moon, and stars and would walk through fire and boiling water for you.
units.literal: King Wen valued friends who ran on his errands; Confucius spoke of friends who could speak of gain and loss. Your servant looks back ashamed at his emptiness and shallowness, yet was once unworthy of your private favor; one word pledged the heart, and ten thousand deaths bring no regret. My stout breast of loyalty and strength still surpasses other men; I swear by sun, moon, and stars and am willing to walk through boiling water and fire.

units.zh: 公又何必終年立敵，懇意相窺，徇一時之襟靈，取四郊之倦弊，今日得其小眾，明日下其危牆，弊師無遺鏃之憂，鄰壤抱剝床之痛。
units.en: Why keep an enemy year on year, probing and testing, indulging a passing mood and draining the weary countryside—winning a skirmish today and storming a crumbling wall tomorrow—until broken armies leave arrows on the field and neighboring lands suffer the ruin the Book of Changes calls "the bed stripped bare"?
units.literal: Why must you stand as enemy year after year, earnestly peering and probing, indulging a moment's temper and drawing on the weariness of the four suburbs—today gaining a small band, tomorrow taking down a perilous wall—so that a ruined army has no worry of leaving arrows behind and neighboring lands embrace the pain of the bed stripped bare?

units.zh: 又慮悠悠之黨，妄瀆聽聞，見仆韜勇枕威，戢兵守境，不量本末，誤致窺覦。
units.en: I fear too that loose tongues in your camp will mislead you: seeing me hoard strength and rest on my reputation, sheathe arms and hold my borders, they may mistake restraint for weakness and tempt you to covetous designs.
units.literal: I also fear that idle factions will rashly pollute what reaches your ears, seeing your servant hide courage and rest on prestige, sheath arms and guard borders, and, without weighing root and branch, mistakenly provoke covetous glances.

units.zh: 且仆自壯歲已前，業經陷敵，以殺戮為東作，號兼並為永謀。
units.en: Moreover, long before my prime I was already plunging among enemies, treating slaughter as spring plowing and calling conquest my lasting design.
units.literal: Moreover, from before my prime your servant has already plunged among enemies, taking slaughter as spring plowing and calling annexation his lasting plan.

units.zh: 及其首陟師壇，躬被公兗，天子命我為群後，明公許我以下交，所以斂跡愛人，蓄兵務德，收燕薊則還其故將，入蒲阪而不負前言。
units.en: When I first mounted the commander's altar and received the ducal regalia in person, the Son of Heaven named me among the feudal lords and you, Illustrious Lord, treated me as an equal friend; since then I have restrained my conduct and cherished my people, husbanded arms and pursued virtue, restored Yan and Ji's former commanders when I took those lands, and kept my word when I entered Puban.
units.literal: When I first ascended the commander's altar and personally received the ducal regalia, the Son of Heaven ordered me as one of the feudal lords and you, Illustrious Lord, allowed me friendship as with an inferior; therefore I restrained my tracks and cherished men, stored up arms and pursued virtue, and when I took Yan and Ji I returned their former generals, and when I entered Puban I did not betray prior words.

units.zh: 況五載休兵，三邊校士，鐵騎犀甲，雲屯穀量。
units.en: For five years my armies have rested while the three frontiers drilled their men; iron cavalry and rhinoceros-hide armor stand massed like clouds, and grain is piled like hills.
units.literal: Moreover, for five years arms have rested and the three frontiers have drilled soldiers; iron cavalry and rhinoceros-hide armor mass like clouds, and grain is heaped like hills.

units.zh: 馬邑兒童，皆為銳將；
units.en: The boys of Mayi are all seasoned commanders;
units.literal: the boys of Mayi are all sharp commanders;

units.zh: 鷲峰宮闕，鹹作京坻。
units.en: the storehouses on Vulture Peak might as well be the capital's granary mound.
units.literal: the palaces on Vulture Peak all serve as the capital's granary mound.

units.zh: 問年猶少於仁明，語地幸依於險阻，有何覘睹，便誤英聰。
units.en: Compare our years and I am still the younger; compare our terrain and I am blessed with natural barriers—what is there for you to reconnoiter that should mislead so keen a mind?
units.literal: Ask about years and I am still younger than your humane clarity; speak of terrain and I am fortunate to rely on peril and obstruction—what is there to spy out that should mislead your brilliant discernment?

units.zh: 況仆臨戎握兵，粗有操斷，屈伸進退，久貯心期。
units.en: Moreover, I have stood at the head of armies and learned something of command; when to bend, when to strike, when to advance or pull back—these choices I have long weighed in advance.
units.literal: Moreover, your servant faces battle and holds the army, and has some rough power of decision; bending and stretching, advancing and retreating, he has long stored these in his heart's intent.

units.zh: 勝則撫三晉之民，敗則征五部之眾，長驅席卷，反首提戈。
units.en: Victory would let me soothe the people of the Three Jins; defeat would still let me rally the Five Divisions; I could drive far and sweep all before me, then wheel about with spear in hand.
units.literal: If victorious I will soothe the people of the Three Jins; if defeated I will levy the hosts of the Five Divisions; driving far in sweeping advance, I will turn my head and raise spear.

units.zh: 但慮隳突中原，為公後患，四海群謗，盡歸仁明，終不能見仆一夫，得仆一馬。
units.en: I only fear ravaging the Central Plain and leaving you a lasting trouble; the world's blame would fall on your reputation for humanity, and in the end you would not capture a single man or horse of mine.
units.literal: I only fear ravaging and striking the Central Plain and making a later trouble for you; the slanders of the four seas would all fall on your humane clarity, and in the end you could not see a single man of mine or obtain a single horse of mine.

units.zh: 銳師儻失，則難整齊，請防後艱，願存前好。
units.en: If elite troops are once broken, they are hard to re-form; guard against later hardship, and let us keep the friendship we once had.
units.literal: If sharp troops should be lost, they are hard to set in order again; I beg you to guard against later hardship and wish to preserve our former good feeling.

units.zh: 矧復陰山部落，是仆懿親；
units.en: To say nothing of the Yin Mountain tribes, who are my own close kin;
units.literal: how much more the tribes of Yin Mountain, who are your servant's close kin;

units.zh: 回紇師徒，累從外舍。
units.en: the Uighur hosts have marched beside my house again and again.
units.literal: the Uighur masters and disciples have repeatedly followed my outer household.

units.zh: 文靖求始畢之眾，元海征五部之師，寬言虛詞，猶或得志。
units.en: Wen Jing sought the hosts of Shibi; Yuan Hai marched the Five Divisions—with empty boasts they still sometimes won their way.
units.literal: Wen Jing sought the hosts of Shibi; Yuan Hai levied the armies of the Five Divisions—with broad words and empty phrases they still sometimes achieved their aim.

units.zh: 今仆散積財而募勇輩，輦寶貨以誘義戎，征其密親，啗以美利，控弦跨馬，寧有數乎！
units.en: Today I scatter my hoarded wealth to recruit warriors, cart treasure to entice the frontier tribes, call up their close kin, and feed them rich reward—who can count the bowmen and horsemen I could field!
units.literal: Now your servant disperses accumulated wealth to recruit bold fellows, carts treasure to entice the righteous barbarians, summons their close kin, feeds them with fine profit—bow in hand, astride horse, can there be any counting them!

units.zh: 但緣荷位天朝，惻心疲瘵，峨峨亭障，未忍起戎。
units.en: Only because I hold office under the Son of Heaven, my heart aches for a worn and afflicted people, and I cannot bear to raise arms along those towering frontier walls.
units.literal: Only because I bear office under the heavenly court, my heart aches for the weary and afflicted, and the towering frontier posts—I cannot bear to raise arms.

units.zh: 亦望公深識鄙懷，洞回英鑒，論交釋憾，慮禍革心，不聽浮譚，以傷霸業。
units.en: I hope you will read my humble intent aright, turn your keen judgment, renew friendship and lay resentment aside, foresee disaster and change your course, and refuse idle talk that would wound your hegemony.
units.literal: I also hope you will deeply know my humble heart, turn your brilliant mirror, discuss friendship and release resentment, consider disaster and change your mind, and not heed floating talk to harm your hegemonic enterprise.

units.zh: 夫《易》惟忌滿，道貴持盈，儻恃勇以喪師，如擎盤而失水，為蛇刻鶴，幸賜徊翔，
units.en: The Book of Changes warns against excess; the Way values holding one's gains. To lean on courage and lose an army is to carry a full tray and spill the water, or to carve legs on a snake—I beg you grant me room to turn aside,
units.literal: The Changes warns only against fullness; the Way esteems holding fullness. If one relies on courage and loses the army, it is like carrying a tray and losing the water, or carving a crane on a snake—I beg you grant me circling flight,

units.zh: 仆少負褊心，天與直氣，間謀詭論，誓不為之。
units.en: I have been narrow-spirited since youth, yet Heaven gave me an upright temper; intrigue and crafty argument I swear never to practice.
units.literal: your servant from youth has borne a narrow heart and Heaven gave him upright spirit; secret plots and crafty arguments he swears never to make.

units.zh: 唯將藥石之譚，願托金蘭之分。
units.en: I offer only words harsh as medicine, and ask to renew the bond we once called kin.
units.literal: I will only offer talk harsh as medicine and stone, and wish to entrust myself to the bond of metal and orchid.

units.zh: 儻愚衷未豁，彼抱猶迷，假令罄三朝之威，窮九流之辯，遣回肝膈，如俟河清。
units.en: If my foolish heart cannot reach you and your mind stays closed, then even exhausting the prestige of three dynasties and every argument the nine schools know would not open your breast—it would be like waiting for the Yellow River to run clear.
units.literal: If my foolish heart is not opened and your breast still deluded, even if one exhausted the prestige of three courts and exhausted the arguments of the nine schools, to send back the liver and diaphragm would be like waiting for the river to clear.

units.zh: 今者執簡吐誠，願垂保鑒。
units.en: Now, brush in hand, I speak plainly and beg your careful regard.
units.literal: Now, holding the bamboo slip, I speak my sincerity and beg you to bestow your safeguarding mirror.

units.zh: 仆自眷私睽隔，翰墨往來，或有鄙詞，稍侵英聽，亦承嘉論，每賜罵言。
units.en: Since our private bond was broken, letters have flown back and forth; some of my words may have been coarse and grated on your ear, yet I have also received your fine replies—and your scolding, which I took as kindness.
units.literal: Since private favor was divided, brush and ink have gone back and forth; sometimes coarse words have slightly offended your brilliant hearing, yet I have also received fine discourse and been repeatedly granted words of scolding.

units.zh: 敘歡既罷於尋戈，焚謗幸蠲其載筆，窮因尚口，樂貴和心，願祛沉閼之嫌，以復塤篪之好。
units.en: Shared joy gave way to drawn swords; let us burn the slanders and erase what the brush recorded. In hardship men still prize honest speech; in friendship they value harmony of heart. Remove the buried grudge between us and restore the old music of pipe and flute.
units.literal: Joy in reunion has already ended in seeking spears; burning slander fortunately cancels what the brush recorded. In extremity one still esteems the mouth; in pleasure one values harmony of heart. I wish to remove the suspicion of deep blockage and restore the good accord of xun and chi.

units.zh: 今者卜於嚬分，不欲因人，專遣使乎，直詣鈴閣。
units.en: Reading the lines of discord in our faces, I will not send another man's words; I dispatch an envoy of my own straight to your command pavilion.
units.literal: Now, divining on the lines of a frown, I do not wish to rely on another person; I specially send an envoy to go straight to your bell pavilion.

units.zh: 古者兵交兩地，使在其間，致命受辭，幸存前誌。
units.en: In antiquity, when two armies met, envoys passed between them at the risk of their lives; fortunately the old chronicles still preserve that precedent.
units.literal: In antiquity when arms clashed between two regions, envoys stood between them, risking life to receive words—fortunately the former records survive.

units.zh: 昔賢貴於投分，義士難於屈讎，若非仰戀恩私，安可輕露肝膈，淒淒丹愫，炳炳血情，臨紙向風，千萬難述。
units.en: Worthies of old prized sworn fellowship; men of honor hate to bow to a feud. Had I not still yearned for your private kindness, how could I lay bare my inmost heart? My loyal breast is desolate, my feeling bright as blood; facing this page into the wind, words fail a thousand times over.
units.literal: Former worthies prized pledging their portion; men of honor find it hard to bow to enmity. If not for looking up in longing for private favor, how could one lightly expose liver and diaphragm? My crimson heart is desolate, my bloody feeling bright; facing the paper toward the wind, a thousand myriad things are hard to tell.

units.zh: 辛卯，以宣徽南院使劉延皓為刑部尚書，充樞密使；
units.en: On xinmao Liu Yanhao, Southern Bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made Minister of Justice and Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner;
units.literal: On xinmao, Liu Yanhao, Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made Minister of Justice and assigned as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

units.zh: 辛亥，製皇第二弟存霸可封永王，第三弟存美可封邕王，第四弟存渥可封申王，第五弟存乂可封睦王，第六弟存確可封通王，第七弟存紀可封雅王。
units.en: On xinhai an investiture edict enfeoffed Cunba as Prince Yong, Cunmei as Prince of Yong, Cunwo as Prince Shen, Cunyi as Prince Mu, Cunque as Prince Tong, and Cunji as Prince Ya.
units.literal: On xinhai, an investiture edict made the Emperor's second younger brother Cunba able to be enfeoffed Prince Yong, the third younger brother Cunmei able to be enfeoffed Prince of Yong, the fourth younger brother Cunwo able to be enfeoffed Prince Shen, the fifth younger brother Cunyi able to be enfeoffed Prince Mu, the sixth younger brother Cunque able to be enfeoffed Prince Tong, and the seventh younger brother Cunji able to be enfeoffed Prince Ya.
